extracted.intended_audience: photographers and photojournalists planning to enter the World Press Photo Contest (2026)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and category definitions for entering the 2026 World Press Photo Contest, including region assignment and format-specific eligibility requirements for Singles, Stories, and Long-Term Projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region of entry / regional judging
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 World Press Photo Contest works with six worldwide regions – Africa; Asia Pacific and Oceania; Europe; North and Central America; South America; and West, Central, and South Asia. Entries are judged in the region in which they were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: a single photograph taken in Canada would be entered into North and Central America in the Singles category. Entrants should determine the appropriate region based on where the work was shot. (Link provided on page: 'Find out more about the regions'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-based category set
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three format-based categories: Singles, Stories and Long-Term Projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories welcome work that documents news and/or aftermaths, sports, nature, and social, political and environmental issues and solutions. Choose the format that matches the submission (single frame; multi-frame story; long-term thematic project).

rubrics_metrics.name: No hierarchy of winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note: There is no hierarchy of winners in each category. All winners are weighted equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners in a category are not ranked (no first/second etc. within a category); treat all category winners as equally weighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singles eligibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Singles — Single frame photographs. All singles must have been shot in 2025. All singles are eligible for the World Press Photo of the Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A singles entry must be a single photograph taken in the calendar year 2025 to be eligible. Any single meeting that requirement is automatically eligible for consideration for Photo of the Year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories eligibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories — Stories can contain between 4 and 10 single frame photographs. All photographs entered into the stories category must have been shot in 2024 or 2025. At least four photographs in a story must have been shot in 2025. All photographs shot in 2025 that are included in the story are eligible for the World Press Photo of the Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story entry must contain 4–10 images. Every image must be from 2024 or 2025, and a minimum of four images must be from 2025. Any images from 2025 within a story are eligible for Photo of the Year consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Term Projects eligibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-Term Projects — Projects on a single theme containing between 24-30 single frame photographs. An entry must contain photographs from at least three different years, and a minimum of six photographs must have been shot in 2025. All photographs shot in 2025 that are included in the project are eligible for the World Press Photo of the Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A long-term project must be thematic and include 24–30 images spanning at least three different years, with at least six images from 2025. Any 2025 images in the project are eligible for Photo of the Year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinued category: Open Format
rubrics_metrics.description: With the 2025 World Press Photo Contest, the Open Format category was discontinued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should not expect an Open Format option for 2026 entries; consult the linked article about changes to the contest for further context.
